title: Murine brain tumor microenvironment immunophenotyping using mass cytometry
protocol: Warm media and serum-free media to 37°C using a water bath.
Label 15 mL conical tubes for the samples, which will be added.
Add 9 mL of media into the labeled 15 mL conical tubes.
Thaw the samples and quench the freezing media.
Place the cryovials into the 37°C water bath for about a minute or until about 80% thawed.
Transfer the thawed cell suspensions into the labeled 15 mL conical tubes.
Centrifuge the cell suspensions for 5 min at 300 × g.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend in 1 mL of medium.
Count the cells using a hemacytometer.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 300 × g and discard supernatant.
Resuspend the cells at 2 × 10^7 cells/mL of warm serum-free media.
Prepare 10 uM (2×) Cell-ID™ Cisplatin working solution.
Thaw Cell-ID™ Cisplatin stock aliquot to 25°C.
Add 2 μL of 5 mM Cell-ID™ Cisplatin stock to 998 μL of warm serum-free media.
Mix well to prepare the 10 μM (2×) working solution.
Incubate for 5 min at 25°C.
Quench by adding warmed media at 5× the volume of the stained cells.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 4 mL of Maxpar® Cell Staining Buffer.
Count the cells using a hemacytometer.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells at a concentration of 1–3 million cells in 50 μL of Maxpar® Cell Staining Buffer.
Transfer the cells to 5 mL polypropylene tubes.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Prepare 50 μL of Fc Block by diluting the lanthanide-conjugated anti-CD16/32 antibody to an appropriate concentration determined by titration.
Resuspend the pellet in 50 μL of Fc Block solution.
Incubate at 25°C for 10 minutes.
Prepare a surface antibody master mix using Maxpar® Cell Staining Buffer and all antibodies except anti-CD206 and anti-Gr-1 as per Table 1, making 50 μL of antibody solution per sample.
Add 50 μL of the surface antibody master mix to the Fc Block-cell suspension.
Gently pipette to mix thoroughly.
Incubate at 25°C for 30 minutes, gently vortexing the tubes halfway through.
Prepare anti-Gr-1 antibody at 2× the recommended concentration determined by titration.
Add 50 μL of anti-Gr-1 and incubate for an additional 30 min at 25°C, gently vortexing the tubes at the 15 min halfway point.
Wash the cells.
Add 2 mL of Cell Staining Buffer.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant.
Repeat washing with Cell Staining Buffer for a total of 2 washes.
Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL of 1× Maxpar® Fix I Buffer.
Incubate for 30 min at 25°C to fix the cells.
Make 100 μL intercellular antibody master mix per sample by adding anti-CD206 to Maxpar® Perm-S Buffer.
Wash the cells.
Add 2 mL of Maxpar® Perm-S Buffer.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant.
Repeat the wash for a total of 2 washes.
Gently resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of intracellular antibody stain.
Incubate for 30 min at 25°C.
Wash the cells two more times as done in step 34.
Prepare 1 mL of 1.6% paraformaldehyde (PFA) per sample from the 16% Paraformaldehyde Aqueous Solution with Maxpar® PBS.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of 1.6% PFA.
Incubate for 20 min at 25°C.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant.
Gently vortex to resuspend the pellet in the residual solution.
Prepare 1 mL intercalation solution per sample by diluting 125 uM Cell-ID™ Intercalator (1,000×) stock solution to 125 nM (1×) with Maxpar® Fix and Perm Buffer.
Add 1 mL of the 1× intercalation solution and gently vortex to mix.
Incubate overnight (12–18 h) at 4°C to label the nucleated cells.
Wash the cells.
Add 3 mL of Maxpar® Cell Staining Buffer.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of Milli-Q water and count the cells.
Add an additional 3 mL to wash the cells and centrifuge at 800 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend the pelleted cells with Milli-Q water containing 0.1× EQ™ Four Element Calibration Beads according to cell count to achieve 8–10 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Filter cells with a 40 μm cell strainer prior to introduction into the Helios™, a CyTOF® System.
Select the time interval for applying the normalization factor.
Note that by default, a 100 s interval is used.
In the CyTOF® Software, select the FCS processing tab.
Select the raw FCS files to concatenate.
Click on the “concatenate” tab.
Check the original data box critically.
Route the name and directory of the new concatenated file.
The normalization process will take place automatically upon concatenation.
